очень сильно утомлять, доводить до крайнего истощения
To cause (something) to become damaged, useless, or ineffective through continued use, especially hard, heavy, or careless use.

examples.text: You're going to wear out that game if you keep playing so rough with it.
He wears a pair of tennis shoes out every summer.

"You never take the trouble to see if he will go without it; your whip is always going as if you had the St. Vitus' dance in your arm; and if it does not wear you out, it wears your horse out; you know you are always changing your horses, and why? because you never give them any peace or encouragement."

That concertina was a wonder in its way. The handles that was on it first was wore out long ago, and he'd made new ones of braided rope yarn. And the bellows was patched in more places than a cranberry picker's overalls.

glosses: To deteriorate or become unusable or ineffective due to continued use, exposure, or strain.

examples.text: The old tractor finally wore out.
My shoes wear out quickly now that I walk to work.
Mr. Simpson adds that the station at Stanmore appears practically unchanged from the time of its opening, even to the L.N.W.R. rubber doormat, which "shows no signs of wearing out."

glosses: To exhaust; to cause or contribute to another's exhaustion, fatigue, or weariness, as by continued strain or exertion.

examples.text: You kids are wearing me out!
Trying to keep up with politics wears me out.
Our physical advantage allowed us to wear the other team out and win.

glosses: To become exhausted, tired, fatigued, or weary, as by continued strain or exertion.

examples.text: I'm wearing out, guys. Time to go to sleep.
They built our railways, but they wore themselves out in the process.

glosses: Of apparel, to display in public.

examples.text: Those sweatpants are great for loafing around the house, but they're not meant to be worn out.

glosses: Of a shirt, to not tuck into the pants; to wear in a casual manner.

examples.text: A dress shirt should be tucked in, but a t-shirt can be worn out.

glosses: To punish by spanking.
To draw or let out wholly; to drain completely.

examples.text: The water was exhausted out of the well.
Moisture of the earth is exhausted by evaporation.

glosses: To empty by drawing or letting out the contents.

examples.text: to exhaust a well
to exhaust a treasury
It takes approximately 8 to 9 minutes to exhaust the tank of air and fill it with water.

glosses: To use up; to deplete, drain or expend wholly, or use until the supply comes to an end.

examples.text: My grandfather seemingly never exhausts his supply of bad jokes.
to exhaust one's resources
to exhaust all possibilities
You're exhausting my patience.
I exhausted my strength walking up the hill.

glosses: To tire out; to wear out; to cause to be without any energy.

examples.text: The marathon exhausted me.
It is a branch that climbs for 11½ miles into the picturesque Wealden hills until, apparently exhausted by the effort, it terminates a mile short of the village of Hawkhurst.

glosses: To discuss thoroughly or completely.

examples.text: That subject has already been exhausted.

glosses: To subject to the action of various solvents in order to remove all soluble substances or extractives.

examples.text: to exhaust a drug successively with water, alcohol, and ether

glosses: To expel (as exhaust).

examples.text: Infections can be reduced further if outside air is exhausted after a single use, rather than re-circulated.
They [the doors between two clean rooms] get connected, and then high-pressure air blasts out anything in between: all the outside atmosphere is exhausted by fresh, clean air.

glosses: To discharge or escape (as exhaust).

examples.text: Steam from both high pressure cylinders exhausts through the respective receiver pipes into cylinders.

Figure 7.13e shows a 4/2 valve that normally has the pressure applied to output 4 while output 3 exhausts through the exhaust port. When activated, the pressure switches to output 3 while output 4 exhausts through the exhaust port.

glosses: A system consisting of the parts of an engine through which burned gases or steam are discharged; see also exhaust system.
The steam let out of a cylinder after it has done its work there.

examples.text: A lovely crisp exhaust: a feeling of almost unlimited power combined with complete freedom of running: and, to crown it all, a most melodious and wholly American chime whistle—these were my immediate impressions as we stormed rapidly out of Göttingen, intent on winning back some of the lost time.

Travellers over the London & North Western main line in bygone days will need no reminder of the pattering of cinders on the carriage roofs, the fountains of sparks from the chimneys at night and the distance from which the exhaust of approaching locomotives could be heard, due to the fierceness of their blast in such conditions.

glosses: The dirty air let out of a room through a register or pipe provided for the purpose.

examples.text: If successful, Edison and Ford—in 1914—would move society away from the[…]hazards of gasoline cars: air and water pollution, noise and noxiousness, constant coughing and the undeniable rise in cancers caused by smoke exhaust particulates.

glosses: An exhaust pipe, especially on a motor vehicle.
Exhaust gas.
Exhausted; used up.

examples.text: Although there are dozens of different types of gems, among the best known and most important are diamond, ruby and sapphire, emerald and other gem forms of the mineral beryl, chrysoberyl, tanzanite, tsavorite, topaz and jade.

glosses: A bright shade of slightly bluish or greyish green, typical of polished jade stones.
A succulent plant, Crassula ovata.
Of a grayish shade of green, typical of jade stones.

The king had no other horse to give him but an old jade, for his six brothers and their men had taken all the other horses, but Ashiepattle did not mind that; he mounted the shabby old nag.

glosses: A bad-tempered or disreputable woman.

examples.text: You alwayes end with a iades tricke, I knowe you of olde.

glosses: To fatigue, tire, or weary (someone or something).

examples.text: [T]he Mind once jaded by an attempt above its Power, it either is diſabl'd for the future, or elſe checks at any vigorous Undertaking ever after, at leaſt is very hardly brought to exert its Force again on any Subject that requires Thought and Meditation.

glosses: To treat (someone or something) like a jade; to spurn.

examples.text: The nere-yet beaten Horſe of Parthia, / We haue iaded out o'th' Field.

glosses: To make (someone or something) contemptible and ridiculous.

examples.text: I do not now foole my ſelfe, to let imagination iade mee; for euery reaſon excites to this, that my Lady loues me.

glosses: Very fine solid particles (smoke, dust) or liquid droplets (moisture) suspended in the air, slightly limiting visibility. (Compare fog, mist.)

examples.text: Our hopes, however, soon vanished; for before eight o'clock, the serenity of the sky was changed into a thick haze, accompanied with rain.

glosses: A reduction of transparency of a clear gas or liquid.
An analogous dullness on a surface that is ideally highly reflective or transparent.

examples.text: The soap left a persistent haze on the drinking glasses.
The furniture has a haze, possibly from some kind of wax.

glosses: Any state suggestive of haze in the atmosphere, such as mental confusion or vagueness of memory.

examples.text:
And is it that the haze of grief
⁠Hath stretch’d my former joy so great?
⁠The lowness of the present state,
That sets the past in this relief?
In my haze of alcohol, I thought for one crazy instant that he had plumbed my secret.

glosses: The degree of cloudiness or turbidity in a clear glass or plastic, measured in percent.

examples.text: Haze is listed as a percent value and, typically, is about 1% for meat film.

glosses: Any substance causing turbidity in beer or wine.

examples.text: Various clarifying and fining agents are used in winemaking to remove hazes.

glosses: To be or become hazy, or thick with haze.

examples.text: Pyramids of clouds now fringed its edge, and the centre had hazed into a sandy mist.

examples.text: […] when the young man whirled his horse, “hazed” Jupiter in circles and belaboured him with a rawhide quirt, […] He ceased his cavortings […]

glosses: In a rodeo, to assist the bulldogger by keeping (the steer) running in a straight line.
To use aversive stimuli on (a wild animal, such as a bear) to encourage it to keep its distance from humans.

examples.text: Hazing a bear involves creating a "negative experience for a bear that seeks out human food or loses its natural avoidance of humans and developed areas," the release said. That involves using non-lethal rubber shotgun slugs, or rubber rounds and noise-deterrent rounds in sequence to scare bears away, according to the release.

examples.text: L’esprit infatigable soutient le corps surmené ; il le relève, défaillant. Loin d’être accablé, écrasé par les besognes du présent, aux courtes heures du repos, il conçoit avec une lucidité merveilleuse les besognes de l’avenir.

glosses: Faire supporter des choses considérées comme un poids, lourd à porter.

examples.text: Il vit, non loin du grand chemin, une femme éplorée […], et un homme furieux qui la suivait. […]. Cet homme l’accablait de coups et de reproches.

Les paysans du Lot, il y a vingt ans, étaient misérables, accablés par les hypothèques dont une prospérité relative, survenue à la suite de la guerre, les libéra.

On chercha, dans le Midi, à les déposséder des biens immeubles qu’ils détenaient […]. La tactique consistait à les accabler d’impôts exorbitants et à en poursuivre le recouvrement d’une manière impitoyable.

glosses: Combler outre mesure quelqu’un, de biens, de grâces, de caresses, de louanges, de politesses, etc.

examples.text: Cependant le juge continuait toujours sa route, rendant avec la plus grande ponctualité des saluts dont on l’accablait sur son passage.

glosses: Mettre à sec en puisant, tarir.

examples.text: Épuiser une fontaine à force d’en tirer de l’eau. - L’armée était si nombreuse que partout où elle campait elle épuisait les fontaines et les ruisseaux.

examples.text: Sur ce sujet, c’est un spécialiste que vous ne saurez épuiser.

examples.text: Sentir ses forces s'épuiser.

examples.text: Ils ne revinrent donc qu’exténués et à demi morts de faim.

glosses: Déformer, blesser en rompant les reins.

examples.text: Si vous lui mettez un fardeau si pesant sur le dos, vous l’éreinterez.

examples.text: Il éreinte tous ses employés.

examples.text: La critique a éreinté la mise en scène.
